**Indikator 1b** is a clinical quality indicator utilized by the [[dansk-kvalitetsdatabase-for-inflammatoriske-tarmsygdomme|Dansk Kvalitetsdatabase for Inflammatoriske Tarmsygdomme]] to evaluate the diagnostic workup standards for newly diagnosed children and youth (aged 0–17) with Inflammatory Bowel Disease (IBD) in Denmark [^src1]. It serves as a central metric for ensuring that pediatric patients receive comprehensive and timely evaluations following their initial hospital contact [^src1].

To fulfill the requirements of Indikator 1b, a patient must undergo three specific examinations within a window of ±12 months from their first hospital contact: a [[gastroskopi]], a [[koloskopi]], and an [[mr-scanning-af-tyndtarm]] (or capsule endoscopy) [^src1]. 

During the reporting period spanning from October 1, 2022, to September 30, 2023, the national fulfillment rate for Indikator 1b was 69% [^src1]. This performance fell short of the established development goal of ≥80% [^src1]. Regional and departmental variations were significant; notably, [[region-nordjylland|Region Nordjylland]] achieved only a 38% fulfillment rate [^src1]. Nationwide, 8 out of 14 departments failed to meet the development target [^src1]. An analysis of the 65 newly diagnosed pediatric patients who did not receive a complete workup on time revealed that 60% of these failures were due to a missing MRI of the small intestine or capsule endoscopy [^src1].

The indicator is governed by the [[styregruppen-for-danibd|Styregruppen for DANIBD]], which periodically reviews its clinical relevance and impact on patients [^src1]. During a recent audit, the steering group debated whether to alter the indicator to spare pediatric patients from invasive examinations, but ultimately chose to maintain the current requirements for the time being [^src1]. The next formal audit of Indikator 1b is scheduled for January 1, 2026 [^src1].
